title: Windows 10 End of Support: What It Means and What to Do
seoTitle: Windows 10 End of Support: What to Do Now | Macbryte Ottawa
description: Windows 10 support has ended, but free security updates continue until October 12, 2027. Plain-language steps to enrol, upgrade, or replace your PC.
excerpt: Your Windows 10 computer still works. Here is what "end of support" really means, how to get free security updates until 2027, and your three options.
quickAnswer: Windows 10 computers keep working after support ended on October 14, 2025. Home users can enrol free in Extended Security Updates (ESU) to keep receiving security fixes until October 12, 2027. Open Settings > Update & Security > Windows Update and click "Enroll now". Microsoft will never phone you about this.

faqs.q: Will my Windows 10 computer stop working?
faqs.a: No. It keeps working and your files stay where they are. What stops, unless you enrol in Extended Security Updates, is the security fixes that protect it from viruses and hackers.

faqs.q: Is Windows 10 Extended Security Updates free?
faqs.a: Yes, there is a free option for home users: let Windows back up your settings to your Microsoft account when you enrol. Microsoft also offers a paid one-time option.

faqs.q: How long do Windows 10 security updates last?
faqs.a: For home users enrolled in ESU, security updates continue until October 12, 2027.

faqs.q: Can my computer upgrade to Windows 11 for free?
faqs.a: Possibly. Open the PC Health Check app from the Start menu to find out whether your computer meets the Windows 11 requirements.

title: The Grandparent Scam: How to Spot It and Protect Your Family
seoTitle: Grandparent Scam in Ottawa: How to Spot It and Stop It | Macbryte
description: How the emergency "grandparent" scam works, the one fact that stops it, what to do if you get the call, and where to report it in Ottawa.
excerpt: A panicked "grandchild" needs bail money and a courier is on the way. Here is how the emergency scam works and the simple steps that stop it.
quickAnswer: If a caller says a grandchild or relative needs cash for bail and asks you to keep it secret, it is a scam. Courts in Canada do not collect bail by phone or courier. Hang up, call your family member on a number you already have, and report it to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre at 1-888-495-8501.

faqs.q: Do courts in Canada ask for bail money by phone?
faqs.a: No. Bail is handled through the court system and people must appear in person. No court sends a courier to collect cash.

faqs.q: What should I do if someone is coming to my home to collect money?
faqs.a: Call 911. A courier coming to collect money for a "relative in trouble" is a fraud in progress.

faqs.q: Where do I report the grandparent scam in Ottawa?
faqs.a: Report it to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre at 1-888-495-8501 and to Ottawa Police at 613-236-1222 (non-emergency), even if you did not lose money.

faqs.q: How can my family protect itself?
faqs.a: Agree on a family code word that only you know, keep family details off public social media, and always call back on a number you already have.

title: CRA Scam Calls and Texts: How to Tell Real from Fake
seoTitle: CRA Scam Calls and Texts: How to Tell Real from Fake | Macbryte
description: The CRA never takes gift cards or Bitcoin, never threatens arrest, and never texts refund links. How to spot and check CRA scams in under a minute.
excerpt: A caller says you owe the CRA and police are on the way. Here is how to tell a real Canada Revenue Agency contact from a scam in under a minute.
quickAnswer: The Canada Revenue Agency never demands payment by gift card, prepaid card or cryptocurrency, never threatens arrest, and never asks for banking details by text or email. If in doubt, hang up and call the CRA yourself at 1-800-959-8281 or check CRA My Account.

faqs.q: Does the CRA accept gift cards or Bitcoin?
faqs.a: No. The CRA does not accept payment by gift card, prepaid credit card or cryptocurrency. Any request to pay that way is a scam.

faqs.q: Will the CRA threaten to have me arrested?
faqs.a: No. The CRA does not use threatening language or say police are coming to arrest you.

faqs.q: Does the CRA send text messages with refund links?
faqs.a: No. A text asking you to click a link to claim a refund or credit is a scam. Delete it without clicking.

faqs.q: How do I check if a CRA call is real?
faqs.a: Hang up, then call the CRA at 1-800-959-8281 or sign in to CRA My Account on canada.ca.

sources.title: Government of Canada: CRA scam alerts

title: Free E-books and Audiobooks with Your Ottawa Library Card (Libby App)
seoTitle: Free Ottawa Library E-books & Audiobooks with Libby | Macbryte
description: Borrow e-books, audiobooks and magazines free with an Ottawa Public Library card and the Libby app. Step-by-step setup for iPhone, iPad, Android and computer.
excerpt: Borrow thousands of e-books and audiobooks free with your Ottawa Public Library card. A step-by-step guide to setting up the Libby app.
quickAnswer: With a free Ottawa Public Library card you can borrow e-books, audiobooks and magazines at no charge using the free Libby app. Install "Libby, the library app", search for Ottawa Public Library, sign in with your card number and PIN, then tap Borrow or Place Hold. Books return automatically, so there are no late fees.

faqs.q: Are e-books from the Ottawa Public Library free?
faqs.a: Yes. With an active Ottawa Public Library card you can borrow e-books and audiobooks at no charge.

faqs.q: What app do I need?
faqs.a: Libby, the library app by OverDrive. It is free on iPhone, iPad and Android, and works in a web browser at libbyapp.com.

faqs.q: Are there late fees for e-books?
faqs.a: No. Borrowed e-books and audiobooks return themselves automatically at the end of the loan.

faqs.q: Can I read library books on a Kindle in Canada?
faqs.a: Kindle library lending is not available in Canada. Many Kobo e-readers can borrow library books directly.

title: What Happens to Your Photos and Accounts? Set Up a Legacy Contact
seoTitle: Apple Legacy Contact & Google Inactive Account Guide | Macbryte
description: Make sure family can reach your photos and accounts. Step-by-step: add an Apple Legacy Contact on iPhone or Mac, and set up Google Inactive Account Manager.
excerpt: Ten minutes now can save your family years of frustration. How to add an Apple Legacy Contact and set up Google Inactive Account Manager.
quickAnswer: On an iPhone, go to Settings > your name > Sign-In & Security > Legacy Contact > Add Legacy Contact, then share or print the access key. Your Legacy Contact needs both the access key and a death certificate to request access. Google users can do the same at myaccount.google.com/inactive.

faqs.q: What is an Apple Legacy Contact?
faqs.a: A person you choose who can request access to your Apple account data, such as photos, messages and notes, after you pass away. They cannot see anything while you are alive.

faqs.q: What does a Legacy Contact need to get access?
faqs.a: Both the access key you share with them and a copy of the death certificate.

faqs.q: Does Google have something similar?
faqs.a: Yes. Google Inactive Account Manager lets you choose people to be notified and given access to selected data if your account becomes inactive.

faqs.q: Should I write down my passwords for my family?
faqs.a: Keep a simple list of which accounts you have and where the access key is stored, but not the passwords themselves. A password manager with an emergency-access feature is safer.

sources.title: Apple Support: How to add a Legacy Contact

title: How to Make Text Bigger on iPhone, iPad, Mac and Windows
seoTitle: How to Make Text Bigger on iPhone, iPad, Mac & Windows | Macbryte
description: Squinting at your screen? Step-by-step settings to make text larger on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows 11 and Windows 10, plus a zoom shortcut for any website.
excerpt: Every phone, tablet and computer can make text larger. Here is exactly where to find the setting on iPhone, iPad, Mac and Windows.
quickAnswer: iPhone or iPad: Settings > Display & Brightness > Text Size. Mac: System Settings > Accessibility > Display > Text size. Windows 11: Settings > Accessibility > Text size. Any website: hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (Mac) and press + to zoom in.

faqs.q: How do I make text bigger on my iPhone?
faqs.a: Open Settings > Display & Brightness > Text Size and drag the slider to the right. For even larger text, use Settings > Accessibility > Display & Text Size > Larger Text.

faqs.q: How do I make text bigger on a Mac?
faqs.a: Go to Apple menu > System Settings > Accessibility > Display > Text size and choose a larger size.

faqs.q: How do I make text bigger in Windows 11?
faqs.a: Go to Start > Settings > Accessibility > Text size, drag the slider, and click Apply.

faqs.q: How do I zoom in on a website?
faqs.a: Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (Mac) and press + to zoom in, - to zoom out, and 0 to reset.
